problem:
Title: Fibonacci $\equiv -1 \mod p^2$

Is there a prime $p > 3$ such that the Fibonacci number $F_{np} \equiv -1 \mod p^2$ for some natural number $n$?  I know none of the first $1000$ primes $> 3$ qualify.

EDIT: In response to Calvin Lin's comment: 
Suppose $n$ is the period mod $p$. Of course the period mod $p^2$ is a multiple of $n$. If $M = \pmatrix{1 & 1\cr 1 & 0\cr}$, so that $M^k = \pmatrix{F_{k+1} & F_k\cr F_k & F_{k-1}\cr}$, that says 
$M^n \equiv I \mod p$, so $M^n \equiv I + p A \mod p^2$ for some matrix $A$
with entries in $\mathbb Z_p$.  Then $M^{kn} \equiv I + k p A \mod p^2$.  If $A = 0$, the period mod $p^2$ is $n$, otherwise it is $pn$.  

Note that $n$ divides $p-1$ (if $p \equiv \pm 4 \mod 5$) or $2p+2$ (if $p \equiv \pm 3 \mod 5$), and in either case is coprime to $p$.  Thus if the period mod $p^2$ is not $pn$, $p$ must be
a Fibonacci-Wieferich prime (see Noam Elkies' answer).

0001 | The set of such primes $p$ is probably infinite but very sparse,
0002 | and there are no such $p We show that $p$ must be a "Fibonacci-Wieferich prime", i.e. a prime for which
0003 | $F_k \equiv 0 \bmod p^2$ for some $k \not\equiv 0 \bmod p$;
0004 | as with ordinary Wieferich primes (primes such as $1093$ and $3511$ for which
0005 | $2^p \equiv 2 \bmod p^2$), the number of such $p \leq x$ is expected
0006 | to grow as $\log \log x$ as $x \rightarrow \infty$.
0007 | Conversely, any Fibonacci-Wieferich prime $p$ will admit a congruence
0008 | $F_{np} \equiv -1 \bmod p^2$.
0009 | 
0010 | Suppose $p>5$.
0011 | Recall that $F_m = (\varphi^m - \overline\varphi^m) / \sqrt{5}$,
0012 | where $\varphi, \overline\varphi = (1 \pm \sqrt5) / 2$
0013 | with $\varphi \overline\varphi = -1$.
0014 | Hence if $F_m \equiv -1 \bmod p^2$ then $\varphi^m \bmod p^2$
0015 | is a root of $X^2 + \sqrt5 \, X - (-1)^m = 0$.
0016 | Thus if $m$ is odd then
0017 | $$
0018 | \varphi^m = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}
0019 | = -\varphi \ \ \text{or} \ \ \varphi^{-1},
0020 | $$
0021 | while if $m$ is even then
0022 | $$
0023 | \varphi^m = \frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}
0024 | = -\varphi^2 \ \ \text{or} \ \ -\!\varphi^{-2}.
0025 | $$
0026 | [This even case is where we must assume $p \neq 3$, because
0027 | the discriminant of $X^2 + \sqrt5 \, X - 1$ is $9 \equiv 0 \bmod 3$,
0028 | so $\phi^m$ can be congruent to one of its roots only modulo 3
0029 | but still satisfy the quadratic equation modulo 9.]
0030 | Thus if $m$ is odd then $\varphi^{m+1}$ or $-\varphi^{m-1}$ is $1 \bmod p^2$,
0031 | while if $m$ is even then $-\varphi^{m+2}$ or $-\varphi^{m-2}$ is $1 \bmod p^2$.
0032 | In each of these four cases, then,
0033 | if $m=np$ then $\varphi^k \equiv 1 \bmod p^2$ for some
0034 | $k$ that is not a multiple of $p$ (namely $k = m+1$, $2m-2$, or $2m\pm 4$).
0035 | This makes $p$ a Fibonacci-Wieferich prime.  The paper
0036 | 
0037 |   Richard J. McIntosh and Eric L Roettger:
0038 |   A search for
0039 |     Fibonacci-Wieferich and Wolstenholme primes,
0040 |   Math. of Computation 76 #260 (2007), 2087-2094.
0041 | 
0042 | explains why we expect the $\log \log x$ behavior, and reports on an
0043 | exhaustive search over $p solutions $m$ of $F_m \equiv -1 \bmod p^2$ should include multiples of $p$.
0044 | 
0045 | Conversely, if $p$ is a Fibonacci-Wieferich prime then there exists some
0046 | even $k \not\equiv 0 \bmod p$ such that $\varphi^k \equiv 1 \bmod p^2$.
0047 | (If the smallest $k$ was odd then double it.)  By "Chinese Remainder"
0048 | $k$ has a multiple $k' \equiv 1 \bmod p$, and this $k'$ is again even with
0049 | $\varphi^{k'} \equiv 1 \bmod p^2$.  Therefore $F_{np} \equiv -1 \bmod p^2$
0050 | with $np = k'-1$ odd, QED.
